question: How do I trace a custom multi-turn agent in Python?
answer:
Use the Weave agent tracing APIs: open a conversation with `weave.start_conversation(...)`, then wrap each user exchange in `weave.start_turn(...)`, with `weave.start_llm(...)` and `weave.start_tool(...)` inside it. These map to the `invoke_agent`, `chat` and `execute_tool` spans. The conversation itself creates no span and only groups turns [S3]. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab [S1].

- **Context managers:** In Python, all four functions work as context managers (`with weave.start_*(...) as obj:`). On exit they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions [S3].
- **Grouping:** The top-level `weave.start_turn(...)` takes the conversation ID from the active conversation. If none is active, the turn has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped with other turns [S2].
- **History is yours to keep:** The quickstart appends each user and assistant message, and each tool result, to a `history` list. It passes that list to the model on every call [S4]. The tracing scopes record activity. They don't replace that history.

Condensed from the quickstart. It needs an OpenAI client and a tool schema, and I haven't run it:

```python
import weave

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model=MODEL):
        with weave.start_llm(model=MODEL, provider_name="openai") as llm:
            resp = openai_client.chat.completions.create(model=MODEL, messages=history)
            msg = resp.choices[0].message
            llm.output(msg.content or "")
            history.append(msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
        # If msg.tool_calls: wrap each call in weave.start_tool(...)
        return msg.content

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="research-bot"):
    history = []
    for q in ["Who founded Anthropic?", "Summarize what we discussed."]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

The full quickstart also shows the tool-call loop and `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...))` for token usage [S4]. If you only want to trace individual functions with `@weave.op`, that is a different workflow [S1].

sources.heading: How the Weave SDK works with agents
sources.text:
## How the Weave SDK works with agents

The Weave SDK includes a generic OTel ingest system for agents, meaning that Weave can capture information from any OTel span in your agent's code. However, Weave requires special handling of the following spans to render your agent's traces in the Agents view of the Weights & Biases UI.

| Concept | Python | TypeScript | OTel span |
| - | - | - | - |
| A conversation | `weave.start_conversation(...)` | `weave.startConversation(...)` | (no span, groups turns) |
| One user or agent exchange | `weave.start_turn(...)` | `weave.startTurn(...)` | `invoke_agent` |
| One LLM API call | `weave.start_llm(...)` | `weave.startLLM(...)` | `chat` |
| One tool execution | `weave.start_tool(...)` | `weave.startTool(...)` | `execute_tool` |

In Python, all four functions work as context managers (`with weave.start_*(...) as obj:`). On exit, they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions. In TypeScript, call `.end()` on each returned object. Use `try { ... } finally { obj.end(); }` to guarantee cleanup on exceptions.

Other [GenAI semantic-convention attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/), such as `gen_ai.usage.*` and `gen_ai.agent.name`, enable additional rendering, but they're optional.

# Quickstart: Set up custom agent observability

> Trace a multi-turn agent with the Weave SDK. Conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool calls render in the Agents view of your project.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/get-started/custom-agents.md).

[Try in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/github/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.ipynb) · [GitHub source](https://github.com/wandb/examples/blob/main/colabs/weave/custom-agents-quickstart.ipynb)

The Weave SDK lets you trace agents built with popular SDKs or custom harnesses. This quickstart shows you how to manually integrate Weave into a custom-built multi-turn agent to emit and capture OpenTelemetry spans. For conceptual understanding about Weave for agents, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

If you're looking to integrate Weave with SDKs or harnesses such as the Claude Agent SDK or Codex, see [Choose an agent integration](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/agent-integration-quickstart.md). Weave autopatches into several agent-building SDKs and agent harnesses for quick integration.

sources.text:
# Trace your agents

> Use the Weave SDK to instrument multi-turn agentic applications and view them in the Agents tab.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tracing/instrument.md).

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

## Multi-turn conversations

Bedrock Agents preserve conversation state on the service side when you reuse a `sessionId`. To group multiple turns into a single trace in the Weights & Biases UI, wrap the turns in `weave.thread`:

```python lines theme={"system"}
with weave.thread("support-conversation") as t:
    for prompt in [
        "I can't log in to my account.",
        "I already tried resetting my password.",
    ]:
        ask_agent(prompt, session_id=t.thread_id)
```

Weave displays each turn in the UI as individual rows in the Threads view.

results.snippet:
### <kbd>method</kbd> `get_agent_turns`

```python theme={"system"}
get_agent_turns(
    conversation_id: 'str',
    limit: 'int' = 50,
    offset: 'int' = 0,
    include_feedback: 'bool' = False
) → AgentConversationChatRes
```

Get the multi-turn chat view for a conversation.

Each turn corresponds to one trace.

**Args:**

* **`conversation_id`**: The conversation whose turns to fetch.
* **`limit`**: Maximum number of turns to return.
* **`offset`**: Number of most-recent turns to skip (for pagination).
* **`include_feedback`**: If true, include feedback on the messages.

**Returns:**
An `AgentConversationChatRes` with the ordered `turns`.

**Example:**

```python theme={"system"}
client = weave.init("entity/project")
resp = client.get_agent_turns(conversation_id="...", limit=20)
for turn in resp.turns:
     for message in turn.messages:
         print(message.type)
```

### When to use agent tracing and when to use application instrumentation

Choose which workflow to use based on what you want to observe:

* **Use agent tracing if you're building or running an agent.** This is the right fit if you use a supported agent harness or agent SDK, or if you've built a custom agent that you can instrument yourself.

* **Use application instrumentation if you're tracing application code.** This is the right fit for applications structured around discrete calls rather than conversations, such as a RAG pipeline, a summarization endpoint, or custom business logic.

Each approach records traces in its own part of the UI: agent traces appear on the **Agents** page, and `weave.op` calls appear on the **Traces** page. You can use both approaches in the same Weave project, but they produce separate traces.

Learn how to instrument a multi-turn agentic application using the W\&B Weave SDK so that you can view, debug, and evaluate your agent's behavior. This guide is intended for developers who build or integrate agents and want structured visibility into conversations, turns, LLM calls, and tool executions.

The Weave SDK for Agents models the full lifecycle of a multi-turn agent conversation: the agent that owns many conversations, the conversation that groups turns together, each user-agent exchange (turn), the LLM calls within a turn, and the tool executions that an LLM triggers. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab of your Weave project. Each conversation shows a multi-turn timeline with nested tool calls, token usage, and feedback.

Weave is built on [OpenTelemetry (OTel)](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/), the open standard for distributed tracing. Every turn, LLM call, and tool call emits an OTel *span* (a structured record of one operation). Each span is tagged with [GenAI semantic-convention](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/) attributes like `gen_ai.agent.name` and `gen_ai.conversation.id`.

If you're tracing individual functions as Ops with the `@weave.op` decorator, see [Trace LLM applications](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md) instead.

result.heading: How the Weave SDK works with agents
result.text:
## How the Weave SDK works with agents

The Weave SDK includes a generic OTel ingest system for agents, meaning that Weave can capture information from any OTel span in your agent's code. However, Weave requires special handling of the following spans to render your agent's traces in the Agents view of the Weights & Biases UI.

| Concept | Python | TypeScript | OTel span |
| - | - | - | - |
| A conversation | `weave.start_conversation(...)` | `weave.startConversation(...)` | (no span, groups turns) |
| One user or agent exchange | `weave.start_turn(...)` | `weave.startTurn(...)` | `invoke_agent` |
| One LLM API call | `weave.start_llm(...)` | `weave.startLLM(...)` | `chat` |
| One tool execution | `weave.start_tool(...)` | `weave.startTool(...)` | `execute_tool` |

In Python, all four functions work as context managers (`with weave.start_*(...) as obj:`). On exit, they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions. In TypeScript, call `.end()` on each returned object. Use `try { ... } finally { obj.end(); }` to guarantee cleanup on exceptions.

Other [GenAI semantic-convention attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/), such as `gen_ai.usage.*` and `gen_ai.agent.name`, enable additional rendering, but they're optional.

input.answer:
Use the Weave agent tracing APIs: open a conversation with `weave.start_conversation(...)`, then wrap each user exchange in `weave.start_turn(...)`, with `weave.start_llm(...)` and `weave.start_tool(...)` inside it. These map to the `invoke_agent`, `chat` and `execute_tool` spans. The conversation itself creates no span and only groups turns [S3]. Traces appear in the **Agents** tab [S1].

- **Context managers:** In Python, all four functions work as context managers (`with weave.start_*(...) as obj:`). On exit they end the span and flush attributes, including on exceptions [S3].
- **Grouping:** The top-level `weave.start_turn(...)` takes the conversation ID from the active conversation. If none is active, the turn has no `conversation_id` and isn't grouped with other turns [S2].
- **History is yours to keep:** The quickstart appends each user and assistant message, and each tool result, to a `history` list. It passes that list to the model on every call [S4]. The tracing scopes record activity. They don't replace that history.

Condensed from the quickstart. It needs an OpenAI client and a tool schema, and I haven't run it:

```python
import weave

def run_turn(history, user_message):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})
    with weave.start_turn(user_message=user_message, model=MODEL):
        with weave.start_llm(model=MODEL, provider_name="openai") as llm:
            resp = openai_client.chat.completions.create(model=MODEL, messages=history)
            msg = resp.choices[0].message
            llm.output(msg.content or "")
            history.append(msg.model_dump(exclude_none=True))
        # If msg.tool_calls: wrap each call in weave.start_tool(...)
        return msg.content

with weave.start_conversation(agent_name="research-bot"):
    history = []
    for q in ["Who founded Anthropic?", "Summarize what we discussed."]:
        run_turn(history, q)
```

The full quickstart also shows the tool-call loop and `llm.record(usage=weave.Usage(...))` for token usage [S4]. If you only want to trace individual functions with `@weave.op`, that is a different workflow [S1].
